scope: Local qualification remediation only; original fixed authorization is not renewed or rearmed

implementation.encryption: AES-256-GCM with a fresh random nonce per record; authenticated source commit, environment, operator, authorization, run, time and key reference
implementation.custody: Explicit injected 32-byte key provider; no automatic environment, Keychain, network or credential discovery
implementation.baseline: Use createDurablePreservationSession so snapshot collector and encrypted baseline share the exact same per-run HMAC key
implementation.persistence: 0700 caller-owned parent/run directories; exclusive run claim; 0600 exclusive no-follow record creation; file and directory fsync; verified decrypt/readback before login and POST
implementation.sequence: One baseline, authorization and single POST intent; encrypted postflight and terminal records; ciphertext hash chain
implementation.recovery: recoverDurablePreservation restores original HMAC key and collects read-only current state; never logs in, arms, retries or submits an event
implementation.health: Mandatory snapshot collection precedes optional health; optional health has bounded timeout; public postflight artifact failure cannot suppress private capture
implementation.exceptions: Missing/corrupt evidence, wrong scope/key, failed persistence and existing runs fail closed; ambiguous intent requires operator reconciliation, never automatic resubmission

trustLimits: An injected provider must retain the key independently of the execution process. Local synthetic key-file tests are not hosted custody approval.

Local encryption/hash chaining does not detect deletion or rollback of an entire valid suffix without an independently retained receipt/anchor. Protect and back up the evidence directory, key and latest receipt under separate custody.
This protects against accidental loss and unauthorized readers without the key; an attacker controlling the same OS identity, runtime and custody provider is outside this local file-store boundary.
Run identity must be allocated and retained by the authorized operator. Do not create a new run to replay an uncertain historical authorization.
No prior missing historical evidence is reconstructed or retroactively accepted by this implementation. PH2-CORE-EVIDENCE-001 remains open.
Snapshot readers and key providers are trusted injected dependencies. Independent review and environment-specific retention/restore drills remain required.
reproduction: npm ci --offline (only with an already approved, populated cache; do not replace the lockfile)
hostedBoundary: No hosted command was introduced or executed. No database, Storage policy, migration or product capability change is required by this remediation.
